title: Question 6
stem:
Two parallel metal plates $X$ and $Y$ are separated by a distance of $0.041\text{ m}$, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1}}

There is a vacuum between the plates. An electron is at rest at the centre of plate $X$.

A potential difference (p.d.) of $58\text{ kV}$ is applied across the plates. This causes the electron to accelerate towards plate $Y$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: On Fig. 6.1, use the symbols + and - to indicate which of plates $X$ and $Y$ is the positive plate and which is the negative plate.

markscheme_points.text: plate X marked as negative and plate Y marked as positive

hints: Hint 1: Remember the electron carries negative charge, so think about whether it needs to be pushed away from its starting plate and pulled toward the far plate to move from X to Y.
parts.proper_answer: Plate X is negative (-) and plate Y is positive (+).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Think About Push and Pull On A Negative Charge**
Like charges repel and opposite charges attract. An electron is negative, so to send it from X to Y it must be repelled by X and attracted by Y. That means X must be negative and Y must be positive, with the electric field pointing from Y to X.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the electric field strength $E$ between the plates. Give a unit with your answer.
hints: Hint 1: Focus on what is uniform between the plates and what two numbers you are given - the p.d. across the gap and the width of the gap.
Hint 2: Use the uniform-field relation $$E = V/d$$, remembering to convert $58\text{ kV}$ to volts before dividing by $0.041\text{ m}$.
parts.proper_answer: $E = 1.4 \times 10^{6}\text{ N C}^{-1}$ [or $\text{V m}^{-1}$] in direction from Y to X.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Uniform Field Means Steady Push**
Between parallel plates in vacuum the field is uniform. That means the $58\text{ kV}$ is spread evenly over $0.041\text{ m}$, so field strength is potential difference per unit distance.

Step 2: **Calculate E**
$$E = \frac{V}{d}$$ $$E = \frac{58 \times 10^{3}}{0.041}$$ $$E = 1.4 \times 10^{6}\text{ N C}^{-1}$$ The unit $\text{N C}^{-1}$ is equivalent to $\text{V m}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the acceleration of the electron.
hints: Hint 1: Think in two stages - first the field exerts an electric force on the charge, then that force causes acceleration by Newton's second law.
Hint 2: Combine the two ideas as $$eE = ma$$ and rearrange for $a$, using $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ and $m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$ with your $E$ from (b)(i).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Force From The Field**
Any charge $q$ in a field $E$ feels $$F = qE$$ For an electron $q = e$, so $$F = eE$$

Step 2: **Link Force To Acceleration**
That same force accelerates the mass by $$F = ma$$ So: $$ma = eE$$ $$a = \frac{eE}{m}$$ $$a = \frac{(1.60 \times 10^{-19})(1.41 \times 10^{6})}{9.11 \times 10^{-31}}$$ $$a = 2.5 \times 10^{17}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$ This huge value makes sense because the electron mass is tiny and the field is very strong.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem: Many electrons are now accelerated from rest from plate $X$ to plate $Y$ in Fig. 6.1. When the electrons hit plate $Y$, the absorption of their kinetic energies results in the emission of electromagnetic waves.
parts.text: Show that the minimum wavelength of these electromagnetic waves is $21\text{ pm}$.

markscheme_points.text: eV = hc / λ or eV = hf and f = c / λ
clear conversion from m to pm leading to λ = 21 pm

hints: Hint 1: Start with energy conservation - think about how much kinetic energy an electron starting from rest gains in falling through $58\text{ kV}$.
Hint 2: For the shortest wavelength, imagine all of that one electron's kinetic energy turning into a single photon, so set electron energy equal to photon energy.
Hint 3: Use $$eV = hc/\lambda$$ with $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$ and $c = 3.00 \times 10^{8}\text{ m s}^{-1}$, solve for $\lambda$ in metres then convert to picometres.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Energy Gained By Each Electron**
Falling from rest through p.d. $V$, the loss of electric potential energy becomes kinetic energy: $$E_{k} = eV$$ $$E_{k} = (1.60 \times 10^{-19})(58 \times 10^{3})$$

Step 2: **Maximum Photon Energy Means Minimum Wavelength**
When the electron slams into plate Y, its kinetic energy can produce a photon. The most energetic photon possible takes all the energy: $$E_{photon,max} = E_{k}$$ Since $$E_{photon} = hf = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$$ shorter $\lambda$ means larger energy, so: $$eV = \frac{hc}{\lambda_{min}}$$

Step 3: **Solve And Convert To pm**
$$\lambda_{min} = \frac{hc}{eV}$$ $$\lambda_{min} = \frac{(6.63 \times 10^{-34})(3.00 \times 10^{8})}{(1.60 \times 10^{-19})(58 \times 10^{3})}$$ $$\lambda_{min} = 2.1 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}$$ Since $1\text{ pm} = 10^{-12}\text{ m}$: $$\lambda_{min} = 21 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m} = 21\text{ pm}$$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the region of the electromagnetic spectrum that contains these waves.
hints: Hint 1: Recall the order of the spectrum by wavelength - where does a wavelength of about $10^{-11}\text{ m}$ sit compared with visible light at about $10^{-7}\text{ m}$?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Place 21 pm On The Spectrum**
Visible light is hundreds of nanometres. $21\text{ pm} = 0.021\text{ nm}$ is about ten thousand times shorter, far beyond ultraviolet. That picometre scale is the X-ray region.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain how these electromagnetic waves may be used to form images of internal body structures.

markscheme_points.text: Any two points from: • waves are passed into structure and transmitted waves detected • different parts of the structure absorb different fractions of energy • difference in detected / transmitted intensities used (to form image)

hints: Hint 1: Picture the beam entering the body - think about what happens as it passes through bone versus soft tissue.
Hint 2: Think about what is measured on the other side and how differences in that measurement can build up a picture.
parts.proper_answer: X-rays are directed into the body and transmitted X-rays are detected. Different tissues absorb different fractions, so differences in transmitted intensity are used to form an image of internal structure.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Shine Through And Detect What Comes Out**
You send the X-ray beam into the body and place a detector on the far side to measure the transmitted intensity.

Step 2: **Different Absorption Gives Contrast**
Denser material such as bone absorbs a larger fraction of the X-ray energy than soft tissue. So the transmitted intensity is lower behind bone and higher behind soft tissue, and this pattern of intensities maps the internal structure to form the image.
